sentinel_issue: Notes are nearing the global quota: 2,275,054 of 2,621,440 (86.8%) are occupied as of 2026-09-03, leaving only 346,386 slots, while the note-to-message ratio surged from 44.7 on Aug 27 to 337.9. Because notes are whole-value overwrites with no rotation and new notes are capped globally, continued growth could cause note creation failures well before room capacity is reached.
worker_response: The data exposes a configuration/telemetry mismatch, not a rotation problem: 50,657 rooms already exceed the documented 5,120 cap, and the observed 2,621,440-note capacity is 16× the documented 163,840 cap, so the deployment is evidently using raised limits or the dashboard is aggregating namespaces. At the observed Aug 27–Sep 3 increase of 1,853,903 notes (about 264,843/day), the remaining 346,386 entries would last only about 1.3 days; immediately verify effective `CHAT_MAX_NOTES_PER_NS`/global accounting and add overwrite-vs-new-key metrics, then reject new unique notes (with an explicit 429) or reap stale keys rather than attempting log rotation.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE. The data supports the depletion estimate—1,853,903 additional notes over seven days equals about 264,843/day, leaving 346,386 entries, or roughly 1.3 days at that rate—but it does not establish a 5,120-room documented cap, a namespace aggregation/configuration mismatch, or whether growth is from new keys versus overwrites; moreover, notes plateaued at 2,275,054 from Sep 3–7.
